gloss: to be proportionate; to correspond; to look at each other

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {見合|みあ}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to be proportionate; to correspond; to be commensurate
definitions.explanation: To be appropriate or in proportion to something. Often used when discussing whether effort, cost, or quality matches expectations or value.

definitions.gloss: to look at each other; to face each other
definitions.explanation: For two people or things to look at or face one another.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}に{見合|みあ}う{結果|けっか}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: The results were commensurate with the effort.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}に{見合|みあ}う{品質|ひんしつ}かどうか{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked whether the quality matched the price.

examples.japanese: このホテルは{料金|りょうきん}に{見合|みあ}うだけのサービスを{提供|ていきょう}している。
examples.english: This hotel provides service worthy of its rates.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{見合|みあ}って{笑|わら}った。
examples.english: The two looked at each other and laughed.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}と{味方|みかた}が{見合|みあ}ったまま{動|うご}かなかった。
examples.english: The enemy and ally faced each other without moving.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}で{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれ、{参加者|さんかしゃ}たちは{顔|かお}を{見合|みあ}わせた。
examples.english: Opinions were divided at the meeting, and the participants looked at each other.

notes:
{見合|みあ}う is an intransitive godan verb.

ASPECT (ている):
{見合|みあ}っている indicates a state of facing each other or being proportionate.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [thing]に{見合|みあ}う (be proportionate to, match)
- [person]と{見合|みあ}う (look at each other)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {値段|ねだん}に{見合|みあ}う (match the price)
- {努力|どりょく}に{見合|みあ}う (be commensurate with effort)
- {給料|きゅうりょう}に{見合|みあ}う (be proportionate to one's salary)
- {顔|かお}を{見合|みあ}わせる (exchange glances)

The phrase {顔|かお}を{見合|みあ}わせる uses the causative form and is a set expression meaning to exchange surprised or confused glances. Distinct from {見合|みあ}い (arranged marriage meeting), which is the noun form of a related but specialized meaning.
